pr_body:
- Add additional fields to `JWTAuthenticator` in `AuthenticationConfiguration` v1alpha1
- Add support for CEL expressions and integrate with OIDC authenticator

fixes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/119235

/kind feature
/sig auth
/triage accepted
/milestone v1.29
/priority important-soon

```release-note
Adds CEL expressions to v1alpha1 AuthenticationConfiguration.
```

```docs
[KEP]: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-auth/3331-structured-authentication-configuration
```

> should feature enablement be checked here?

we are checking for feature enablement in `validation.go`. `New` method that constructs the authenticator gets the compiled CELMapper for validation and if the feature is not enabled, the subfields are nil.

> I was hoping it would be more obvious that existing code paths were intact if the feature gate was disabled or no CEL capabilities were used in the config, either via a pattern like

We are following this pattern here.
1. If expressions are set and feature gate isn't enabled, we get an error from `CompileAndValidateJWTAuthenticator` and fail to create an Authenticator.
2. If expressions are set and feature gate is enabled, we have mappers for the subfields which contain expressions.
   - I've moved the username and groups computation code to their own functions, `getUsername` and `getGroups` respectively.  Within those functions, we have the old code as-is and the new code is inside an if loop if the subfield mapper isn't `nil`.
   - `getUID`, `getExtra` is net new code that didn't exist before.
   - `claimValidationRules` is an array and can contain a mix of the old (`.claim` and `.requiredValue`) and new (`.expression` and `.message`). The old code is kept as-is and we have added check with cel expressions if the subfield is not nil.
   - `userValidationRules` is net new, so that has been added now.

There is a lot of `if feature-enabled` checks in the validation code to guard against:
1. using expressions in username, groups claim mapping, claim validation when feature gate not set
2. using UID, Extra claim mapping when feature gate not set 
3. using user validation rules when feature gate not set

non-blocking since this doesn't touch the config API layer, but ClaimsMapper is a really confusing interface... each instance held in `CELMapper` is only valid to call one of the methods. It's weird to have to put the documentation about which uses of this interface should call which methods on the interface doc.

interaces like these would be clearer (even if the names get a little silly by the end):
```go
Username             StringMapper
Groups               StringArrayMapper
UID                  StringMapper
Extra                MapStringStringArrayMapper
ClaimValidationRules BoolMapper
UserValidationRules  BoolMapper
```

```go
type BoolMapper interface {
  MapBool(context.Context, *unstructured.Unstructured) (bool, error)
}
type StringMapper interface {
  MapString(context.Context, *unstructured.Unstructured) (string, error)
}
type StringArrayMapper interface {
  MapStringArray(context.Context, *unstructured.Unstructured) ([]string, error)
}
type MapStringStringArrayMapper interface {
  MapMapStringStringArray(context.Context, *unstructured.Unstructured) (map[string][]string, error)
}
```

specific implementations of those could wrap an interface like
```
EvalSingle(context.Context, *unstructured.Unstructured) (EvaluationResult, error)
```
or
```
EvalMultiple(context.Context, *unstructured.Unstructured) ([]EvaluationResult, error)
```
and type-check / accumulate

I think this could be cleaned up in 1.30 to be a lot more composable
